query: For high-entropy-alloy coatings used in wear-resistant applications, what single intervention could improve wear resistance across operating temperatures? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its expected mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise identical unmodified coating, the temperature and sliding conditions under which it should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and an experiment with a clear result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of TiC to a high-entropy alloy coating will improve its wear resistance across operating temperatures.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal amount of TiC to be added and the potential effects of TiC on the corrosion resistance of the coating

falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear rate of the TiC-modified coating is not significantly lower than that of the unmodified coating, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The AlCoCrFeNiSi HEA coating showed a volume wear rate of (0.38 ± 0.08) × 10−4 mm3·N−1·m−1, which is about half that of the AlCoCrFeNiTi coating in our previous study (0.77 ± 0.01) × 10−4 mm3·N−1·m−1 [] at the same test conditions. This result indicates that the wear resistance of the AlCoCrFeNiSi coating was better than that of the AlCoCrFeNiTi coating. Besides, comparing with the conventional flame-sprayed NiCrBSi coating with a volume wear rate of about 1.7 × 10−4 mm3·N−1·m−1 [], the coating in this paper also showed much better wear resistance. All of these results make the APS AlCoCrFeNiSi coating a promising one that can be used in abrasion environments in the industries of petroleum, power, mining, and so on. Besides the high density of the coating and the high hardness of the AlCoCrFeNiSi material, formation of the hard tribofilms (Figure 13) can be another reason for the good wear resistance.

One of the most investigated HEA systems is AlCoCrCuFeNi and the copper-free derivate AlCoCrFeNi [,]. Distinct improvement of mechanical properties can be achieved by alloying with titanium. Due to its large atomic radius, the addition of titanium causes solid–solution strengthening and hence increased strength and hardness. Additionally, the formation of brittle phases was observed for a high content of titanium [,,]. The wear resistance of the alloy system AlCoCrFeNiTi has been investigated under various conditions revealing an increased wear resistance, also in comparison with the steels EN 1.3505 and EN 1.3343 [,]. Although improved high-temperature properties of AlCoCrFeNiTi are expected, the wear behaviour has not yet been investigated at increased temperature.

Introduction of ceramic particles is an effective way to improve the wear resistance of the alloys [,,,,,]. For example, the addition of TiB2 in the matrix of (AlCrFeMnV)90Bi10 high-entropy alloy reduced the wear rate by 85%, which significantly improved the wear resistance of the material []. TiC is often used as a reinforcing agent due to its high hardness, high melting point, good wettability, and chemical stability [,,,,,,,]. Adding TiC into the CoCrNi alloy to form a CoCrNi/TiC composite will play the advantages of CoCrNi and TiC, and is expected to form a new type of wear-resistant material. However, there is no relevant report on the improvement of wear resistance by adding TiC into CoCrNi alloys. The purpose of this investigation is to produce a highly wear-resistant CoCrNi/TiC composite, and this idea was verified by experiments. The effects of TiC content on microstructure, mechanical properties, and wear resistance of CoCrNi alloy were investigated.
